answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond before it can vote or claim rewards, then slash that bond when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. One person can still create a comet, sparrow, or oasis of fake identities, but each identity ties up capital and risks losing it; splitting a fixed budget across many accounts also makes every account less influential. The mechanism raises the attacker’s cost rather than pretending identities can be perfectly counted.
